originalGroup.material:
Mixed Pace Walk And Biscuit Stall · Reading

Our walking club welcomed new members, but the first group walk revealed a difficulty. Faster walkers reached every turning well before the others. They waited, then immediately set off again. ____1____ By the time the slower members arrived, the people at the front had rested while those at the back had not.

The leader asked everyone to discuss the problem before the next outing. We agreed that a pause would begin only after the whole group had reached the meeting point. ____2____ Nobody had to use the waiting period as a race to earn a longer break.

We also chose a person to remain at important turnings until the last walker had passed. ____3____ The task was to make the route clear, not to decide that everyone else ought to remember the map.

Some members worried that this would prevent them enjoying a faster pace. The leader explained that separate faster walks could still be arranged. ____4____ A particular outing could have a shared purpose without becoming the only kind of walk the club ever offered.

The next trip was not free of small delays, but it felt more like a group activity. ____5____ We had changed the organisation of the walk instead of treating one pace as a personal failing.

Mixed Pace Walk And Biscuit Stall · Grammar

At our town's food fair, my aunt sold biscuits from a recipe that her mother ____1____ (USE) for many years. I helped her prepare the table and write the price cards. She asked me ____2____ (LEAVE) enough space between the trays so that the labels could be read.

A customer ____3____ recognised the recipe name asked whether the biscuits were exactly like the ones he remembered. My aunt said that she had changed the size, but kept the main ingredients the same. The biscuits were ____4____ (SMALL) than those in an old family photograph.

We spoke ____5____ (CLEAR) about what was in each tray. If we were unsure about a question, we asked the organiser rather than inventing an answer. My aunt said that knowing a family recipe did not mean knowing everything about every customer's needs.

After ____6____ (SERVE) the busiest group, we checked the remaining stock. One tray ____7____ (LABEL) with the wrong price, so we corrected it before another sale. The mistake did not change what a customer had already paid.

At the end, my aunt thanked ____8____ (WE) all for helping. We packed the cards with the recipe notes so we could remember ____9____ had worked well. Next year, we hope ____10____ (USE) a clearer arrangement from the beginning.

options.text: Members could see that the arrangement recognised the experience of those at the back.
That gave everyone a genuine pause before the group moved again.
This walk had been advertised as suitable for people walking together at different speeds.
The same stop therefore gave different people different amounts of rest.
The club decided to ban every fast walk for the rest of the year.
The last person to arrive had to leave first without stopping.
A clear signal at a junction reduced the chance of someone following the wrong path.
